368869.title: Zhao's bipartite swapping conjecture
368869.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph and let $q\geq 2$. Write $K_q$ for the complete graph on $q$ vertices, and let $H\times K_2$ denote the categorical product with the two-vertex complete graph. **Zhao's bipartite swapping conjecture.**

$$
\hom(H,K_q)^2 \leq \hom(H\times K_2,K_q).
$$

This inequality is a proposed bipartite-swapping property for proper $q$-colourings. The paper states that it remains unknown in general, although it is proved for several classes of graphs later in the paper.

368871.title: Universal bipartite-swapping conjecture for antiferromagnetic graphs
368871.statement:
Let $G$ be an antiferromagnetic graph, and let $H$ be any graph. **Universal bipartite-swapping conjecture.** Then

$$
\hom(H,G)^2 \leq \hom(H\times K_2,G).
$$

Here $H\times K_2$ is the categorical product with the two-vertex complete graph. The conjecture would unify the paper's bipartite-swapping results and implies both the Zhao conjecture and the Sah–Sawhney–Stoner–Zhao conjecture. It is presented as an open question in the concluding remarks.

368976.title: The Feynman-period characterization of Speyer's invariant
368976.statement:
A graph is **cyclically $6$-connected** if it is $4$-regular and has no $4$-edge cut other than one isolating a vertex; cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graphs are defined analogously. For such a graph $G$, let $\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}(G)$ denote its Feynman period after deleting any vertex, and let $\mathsf{N}_2(G)$ be the second Speyer invariant.

**Period--Speyer conjecture.** If two cyclically $6$-connected $4$-regular graphs, or two cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graphs, satisfy

$$
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}(G_1)=\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}(G_2),
$$

then

$$
\mathsf{N}_2(G_1)=\mathsf{N}_2(G_2).
$$

This would make $\mathsf{N}_2$ a function of the Feynman period on these graph classes. It is supported by all graphs with known periods but remains open.

369233.title: The three-sevenths upper-bound conjecture for the game isolation number
369233.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $n(G)$ denote its order, and let $\iota_{\rm g}(G)$ and $\iota_{\rm g}'(G)$ denote its game isolation number and Staller-start game isolation number, respectively. A graph has no $K_2$-components when none of its connected components is isomorphic to $K_2$.

**Three-sevenths upper-bound conjecture.** For any graph $G$ with no $K_2$-components,

$$
\iota_{\rm g}(G) \leq \left\lceil\frac{3}{7}n(G)\right\rceil \quad\text{and}\quad \iota_{\rm g}'(G) \leq \left\lceil\frac{3}{7}n(G)\right\rceil.
$$

The paper presents this as a conjecture from earlier work and studies refinements and examples showing that the three-sevenths bound is sharp for suitable graph families. Its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.

369243.title: Finiteness of simultaneous duplicates for separated exponents
369243.statement: Let $k<k'$ be positive integer parameters, and let $f_k(n)$ count the gleeful representations of $n$ with parameter $k$. **The separated-exponent finiteness conjecture.** If $k\ge 3$ or $k'\ge 5$, then there are finitely many integers $n$ with both $f_k(n)>1$ and $f_{k'}(n)>1$. This complements the conjectured infinite families for $(k,k')=(2,3)$ and $(2,4)$; the claim is motivated by the stated heuristic and remains open.

369271.title: Räty–Sudakov–Tomon surplus conjecture for graphs far from clique unions
369271.statement:
Let $G$ be a regular graph on $n$ vertices, with max-cut surplus $\mathsf{sp}(G)$. Say that $G$ is **$epsilon$-far** from a graph $H$ if no graph isomorphic to $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by adding or removing at most $epsilon |V(G)|^2$ edges.

**Räty–Sudakov–Tomon conjecture.** For any $epsilon>0$, there exists a $c>0$ such that, if $G$ is $epsilon$-far from every disjoint union of cliques, then

$$
\mathsf{sp}(G) geq c n^{5/4}.
$$

This conjecture predicts a polynomial improvement over Edwards' bound for regular graphs that are far from the natural low-surplus examples. The supplied text gives no resolution; the cited work establishes a related lower bound with a logarithmic loss in a restricted very dense regular setting.

369354.title: DeBiasio–Han–Lo–Molla–Piga–Treglown conjecture on Turánable oriented graphs
369354.statement:
Let $H$ be an oriented graph. For integers $a,b,c\geq 1$, let $D_{a,b,c}$ be the tournament obtained from the consistently oriented triangle $C_3$ by replacing its vertices with transitive tournaments on $a$, $b$, and $c$ vertices; write $D_s=D_{s,s,s}$.

**DeBiasio–Han–Lo–Molla–Piga–Treglown conjecture.** The oriented graph $H$ is Turánable if and only if there is an $s\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $H\subset D_s$.

The conjecture proposed a characterization of Turánable oriented graphs, motivated by the corresponding theorem for tournaments. It is refuted in the source paper: a Turánable oriented graph exists that is not a subgraph of $D_s$ for any $s\in\mathbb{N}$.

369359.title: Equitable full-cookie distribution conjecture
369359.statement:
Let $r$, $n$, and $m$ be positive integers. A group of $r$ children has $n$ cookies, each with some amount of one or more of $m$ possible kinds of frosting.

**Equitable distribution conjecture.** It should be possible to cut at most $(r-1)m$ cookies and distribute them so that each child has the same amount of each kind of frosting and at least

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n-m(r-1)}{r}\right\rfloor
$$

full cookies.

The bound would be optimal because an equitable distribution of all full cookies can give each child at most $\left\lfloor\frac{n-m(r-1)}{r}\right\rfloor$ full cookies. The conjecture strengthens the paper's theorem by improving its guaranteed number of full cookies while retaining the optimal cut bound.

369576.title: Frankl's conjecture on shattering in antichains
369576.statement:
Let $2^{[n]}$ denote the family of all subsets of $[n]$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is an **antichain** if no two members satisfy $F\subseteq F'$.

**Frankl's conjecture.** Let $k$ be a non-negative integer and $n\geqslant 2k$. If $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is an antichain with $\mathcal{F}\not\rightarrow(k+1,2^{k+1})$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leqslant\binom{n}{k}.
$$

Frankl proved the conjecture for $k\leqslant 2$, and Anstee and Sali proved it for $k=3$; the general case remains open.

369594.title: The algebraic-connectivity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
369594.statement:
Let $a(G,X)$ denote the algebraic connectivity of a graph $G$ in a normed space $X$, let $K_{2d}$ be the complete graph on $2d$ vertices, and let $T_d$ be the tree defined in the paper. **Algebraic-connectivity conjecture.**

$$
a(K_{2d},\ell_\infty^d)=a(T_d)\quad\text{for }d\geq 4.
$$

This conjecture compares the algebraic connectivity of the complete graph in the $d$-dimensional $\ell_\infty$ space with that of the specified tree $T_d$; the supplied excerpt gives no resolution status.

369627.title: The Fibonacci upper-bound conjecture for source-to-sink paths
369627.statement: Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$ for $n 3$. Consider a 3-regular, 3-edge connected, acyclic directed graph with a unique source and a unique sink on $2n$ vertices. **Fibonacci upper-bound conjecture.** Such a graph has at most $F_{n+2}+1$ source-to-sink paths, where $F_{n+2}$ denotes the $(n+2)^{\mathrm{th}}$ Fibonacci number. This removes the planarity restriction from the cited planar conjecture; the optimal graph is described as the wedge of an $(n+1)$-gon over an edge, but the asserted bound remains open in the source.

369861.title: The extremal upper-bound conjecture for the exponential hyper-Zagreb index
369861.statement:
Let $G\in\mathcal{G}_{n,m}$ be a connected graph with $n\geq 6$ and

$$
m=nk-\binom{k+1}{2}+a,
$$

where $1\leq k\leq n-1$ and $0\leq a<n-k-1$. Let $F(G)$ denote the function in the statement. **The extremal upper-bound conjecture.** The function $F(G)$ satisfies

$$
F(G)\leq k(n-1)^3+a(k+1)^3+(n-k-a-1)k^3+(k+a)^3.
$$

This is an upper-bound claim for a graph invariant over connected graphs with fixed order and size; the supplied text gives no resolution or further information about the extremal graphs attaining equality.

369891.title: The weak happy edge conjecture for plane spanning trees
369891.statement: Let $S$ be a convex point set, and let $T_{\text{in}}$ and $T_{\text{tar}}$ be plane spanning trees on $S$. An edge is **happy** if it belongs to both $T_{\text{in}}$ and $T_{\text{tar}}$. **Weak happy edge conjecture.** There is a shortest flip sequence from $T_{\text{in}}$ to $T_{\text{tar}}$ that does not flip happy edges. This conjecture asks whether shortest reconfiguration sequences can preserve all edges common to the initial and target trees. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

369892.title: The parking edge conjecture for plane spanning trees
369892.statement: Let $S$ be a convex point set, and let $T_{\text{in}}$ and $T_{\text{tar}}$ be plane spanning trees on $S$. A **parking edge** is an edge appearing in a flip sequence that is not contained in $T_{\text{in}}\cup T_{\text{tar}}$. **Parking edge conjecture.** There is a shortest flip sequence from $T_{\text{in}}$ to $T_{\text{tar}}$ that only uses parking edges from the boundary of the convex hull of $S$. The conjecture restricts temporary edges in shortest flip sequences to the convex-hull boundary; the supplied text states that a compatible-flip analogue is proved, but does not state that this original unrestricted-flip conjecture is resolved.

369934.title: Dewdney's circuit-and-enumeration conjecture for (m,n)-trees
369934.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $0\leq m\leq n-1$, and let $K$ be a pure $n$-simplicial complex. Write $\alpha_k(K)$ for the number of $k$-simplices of $K$, and call a sequence an $(m,n)$-circuit when it has the circuit property used in Dewdney's definition. **Dewdney's conjecture.** The complex $K$ is an $(m,n)$-tree if and only if it has the following two properties: no $(m,n)$-circuits, and, for some $1\leq k\leq m$, 

$$
\alpha_k(K)=\frac{\alpha_0(K)-m-1}{n-m}\binom{n+1}{k+1}-\frac{\alpha_0(K)-n-1}{n-m}\binom{m+1}{k+1}.
$$

Dewdney posed this as an unresolved structural characterisation of $(m,n)$-trees; the source does not report a resolution.

369971.title: Convergence conjecture for the Temperley–Lieb algebra rewriting system
369971.statement:
Let $n$ be the rank parameter of the presented Temperley–Lieb algebra, with generators $\delta,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}$. Consider the rewriting system on words in $\{\delta,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}\}$ whose rules are

$$
e_i\delta\to\delta e_i,\qquad e_i^2\to\delta e_i,
$$

$$
e_i e_{i\pm1}e_i\to e_i,\qquad e_i e_j\to e_j e_i\text{ if }j<i-1.
$$

**Convergence conjecture.** This rewriting system is convergent, meaning that it is terminating and confluent.

If true, every word has a unique normal form, yielding an algorithm for reducing words and thereby solving equality in the presented Temperley–Lieb algebra.

370133.title: The minimally rigidity-connected stress-independence conjecture
370133.statement:
Let $G$ be a minimally $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected graph, meaning that $G$ is $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected and deleting any edge destroys $\mathcal{R}_d$-connectedness.

**Minimally $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected stress-independence conjecture.** Every minimally $\mathcal{R}_d$-connected graph is $d$-stress-independent.

The statement is known in dimension $d=2$ from the preceding discussion, and the conjecture asks whether it extends to all dimensions.

370420.title: Determination of corona cycles by Laplacian permanental polynomials
370420.statement: Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_1$ be the one-vertex graph, and let $C_n\odot K_1$ denote their corona product. A graph is **determined by its (signless) Laplacian permanental polynomials** if no non-isomorphic graph has the same Laplacian and signless Laplacian permanental polynomials. **Cycle-corona determination conjecture.** For $n\ge 6$, the graph $C_n\odot K_1$ is determined by its (signless) Laplacian permanental polynomials. This conjecture concerns whether the pair of Laplacian and signless Laplacian permanental polynomials characterizes these corona graphs among graphs up to isomorphism. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

370430.title: The oriented strong embedding conjecture
370430.statement:
A graph is **2-connected** if it is connected and has no cut vertex. A **strong embedding** of a graph on a surface is an embedding in which every cell is bounded by a cycle. An **orientable surface** is a surface with an orientation.

**Oriented strong embedding conjecture.** Every $2$-connected graph has a strong embedding on some orientable surface.

This is a long-standing open problem in topological graph theory concerning the existence of strong embeddings for 2-connected graphs.

370734.title: Raspaud–Wang conjecture on partitioning triangle-free planar graphs
370734.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple triangle-free planar graph. A partition of $G$ into an independent set and a forest means that there is a partition $(V_1,V_2)$ of $V(G)$ such that $G[V_1]$ is independent and $G[V_2]$ is a forest. **Raspaud–Wang conjecture.** Every triangle-free planar graph can be partitioned into an independent set and a forest. This would strengthen the known partition of triangle-free planar graphs into two forests; the conjecture is also independently attributed to Kawarabayashi and Thomassen in the surrounding discussion, while the paper presents it as an earlier conjecture of Raspaud and Wang.
